I can climb up the steps.
But I cannot climb down again.
I can climb on a chair.

Papa laughs. “Sonu, learn to climb down!” he says.
I am afraid. But I do not cry.
Slowly, I get down from the table, and down from the chair.
At last, I have learnt to climb down too!

pages.text: Bunty loves to play with butterflies...
...and with birds.
She loves to play with paper boats.
She also likes to make sand castles.

When Bunty goes back home,

her mother asks her to clean up.

But she refuses.
"I hate soaps!" she screams.

image.alt: Girl with dirt on her face kicking a bar of soap

pages.text:
One night, she has a dream.

The germs are all around her castle, and are attacking her.

Bunty is chased by the germs.

She runs for her life and screams, “Help... Help!”

Suddenly, Soap King Bubbly appears.

“Bunty, don't be afraid,” he says. “Go attack the germs!”

the Soap King orders his army of bubbles.
The army of bubbles chases the germs away.

These days, Bunty likes to use soap,

and she brushes and scrubs herself clean.

image.alt: Happy woman looking at child brushing

Who chased the germs away?
Why does Bunty like soap now?

pages.text: Hello, I am the fourth one in the line. Can you see me?

image.alt: Child watching a row of ants

pages.text: Left, right, left, right. We walk silently in a line.

image.alt: Girl and dog watching a row of ants

pages.text: I just got an idea. I am going to get a set of WHEELS to move faster!
We are not noisy like other animals. Ours is a language of smells.

image.alt: Ants feasting on a lollipop while a child, dog and cat wail

pages.text: One kind of smell says, “Follow me this way for a feast.”
Another smell says, “Danger! Do not go there.”

image.alt: Floor being wiped, ants crawling away

pages.text: I love cakes and all kinds of sweets, just like you.

image.alt: Ants feasting on an assortment of sweets

pages.text: Want to see my muscles at work? I may look very tiny to you, but I am very strong.

image.alt: Ant carrying a round, green object

pages.text: Never mind if the door is shut. I can slip through the smallest crack.

image.alt: Ants crawling towards a shelf filled with food

pages.text: Believe it or not, hundreds of us live happily in a colony.

LET US LEARN SOME NEW WORDS.

Small - Big

Slow - Fast

Short - Tall

Thin - Fat

Hard - Soft

Noisy - Quiet

Here are some words with their opposites. Can you make a sentence for each pair of opposite words?

For example, ‘An ant is small; an elephant is big'.

“As busy as an ant” is a nice way to describe someone who is very hard working.

pages.text:
It's hard to be still,

it's hard to be quiet.

It's hard to say no,

to toes that wiggle so.

It's hard to keep down

these merry feet,

When sounds all around tap a happy beat.

Cheep, cheep, cheep call the sparrows.
Drip, drip, drip goes the tap.
SHEE... SHEEEE...

image.alt: Girl and a bird drinking water

pages.text: SHEE... sings the cooker.

Crunch, crunch, crunch...

... uh oh, I know what that is!
“Why little one, have you wandered so far, away from your books, your toys and your cars? Why indeed? There's nothing here to hear or to see.”

I look up at mamma. I look in surprise. Can she not see?

Can she not hear? The cheep, the drip, the sheee...
... and the crunch? A world full of sounds, all waiting to be found?

glossary.note: a pot that whistles when it cooks

questions.q: What goes "drip, drip, drip"?
What sings "SHEE"?

pages.text: Crocky the crocodile was sad.
He had no friends to play with.
Babloo, the butterfly said, "I will play with you, Crocky. Do not cry."
Tutoo, the turtle said, "I will play with you, Crocky. Do not cry."
Susie, the snake said, "I will also play with you, Crocky. Do not cry."
Fred, the frog and Fenny, the fish also came to play.
So, Crocky found new friends to play with. He became happy.

questions.q: Why was Crocky sad?
choices: He had no friends to play with

How did the other animals help Crocky?

pages.text:
Mother's song was soft and sweet.

Chandu was listening to it. Chandu fell asleep.

In his dream, he was flying.

Flying, flying into a garden. Look! A butterfly, so pretty.

The butterfly said, “Well, hello! How are you?”

“Fine, thank you,” Chandu replied.

Chandu flew a bit higher. Flying, flying. He flew into a sparrow.

“Hi there! How do you do?” she asked.

“Very well, thank you,” Chandu said.

Then Chandu soared still higher. Flying, still flying, he met an eagle.

“Hello friend! How are you?” the eagle asked.

“I feel good,” replied Chandu.

Chandu was flying higher and higher. It seemed so easy. Flying, flying. So high that he came up to an aeroplane.

“Hey, Chandu, how do you do?” the aeroplane asked.

“Fine. And safe journey!” Chandu quickly replied.

Soon Chandu climbed higher than before. Flying and still flying.

A rocket came to meet him. “Hello sir, how do you do?” the rocket shouted.

“Very well,” Chandu smiled.

Still, Chandu was flying higher and higher. Now the stars were twinkling all around. They were smiling at Chandu, as though he were a part of them.

“How are you feeling Chandu?” one star asked him.

“I am feeling great!” he said.

Suddenly, the stars began to wobble. And shake.

image.alt: Flying boy with stars around him

pages.text:
It was Mother, shaking Chandu awake. “Good morning, how are you?”

He hugged her hard and said, “Oh, now I feel better than ever before!”

questions.q: What was Chandu doing in his dream?
What did Chandu meet after the eagle?
Why did the stars seem to wobble and shake?

pages.text:
One day, grandfather gave my brother and me some money.

"Go and buy books," he said.

We were both very happy. We both love to read.

Should we go now? Should we go later?

Should we go today? Should we go tomorrow?

We decided to go right now.

Should we go to the big market? Should we go to the small shop?

Should we go with somebody? Should we go alone?

We decided to go to the small shop, just the two of us.

We like the small bookshop. It is small but it has many books.

The man in the shop likes us. He always helps us.

image.alt: Man talking to children in a bookshop

pages.text:
Should I buy a book with a lot of pictures?

Should I buy a book with many stories?

Should I buy a thin book?

I could not decide.

We do not know which book to buy. The man in the shop smiled at us. “Relax, come with me,” he said. “These books are about animals. Those are about machines. Those over there are about wars. Take what you want.”

I picked up some books. My brother picked up some books.

I sat on the floor. He sat on the chair.

And we read and we read and we read.

It was very quiet. There was no sound.

One hour passed. Two hours passed.

Finally, we knew which books to buy.

The man in the bookshop smiled at us. I got a fat book with many stories. My brother got a big book with many pictures.

We ran home to our grandfather. We climbed on his bed.

He put his arms around us and then we read, and read, and read.

image.alt: Man watching children at a bookshop

questions.q: Who gave the children money?
Where did they decide to go?
Why did it take so long to choose?

pages.text:
I am Goloo the circle.

Everyone likes me.

You can find me

everywhere, any time!

image.alt: Children holding hands and forming a circle

pages.text:
The sun looks like me.

When it's too hot,

you need an umbrella which also

looks like half of me.

At night, the moon

looks like me with a smile.

I look at it through

the owl's round eyes.

image.alt: Owl on a tree on a half moon night

pages.text:
Huge watermelons, apples, oranges, tomatoes,

even the tiny lemons - all look like me... and mithai!

Juicy rasgullas, syrupy gulabjamuns, lovely laddus...

are among the many sweets that look like me.

Animals want me to decorate them.

The cheetah, the chital deer,

have me all over their skin.

I'm there on ladybirds and butterflies too!

In the playground,

I'm there as a ball,

a hoopla ring and

many other joyful games!

Why, your trucks,

aeroplanes, cars, cycles,

would not be able to move...

if it weren't for me.

And yet there is one place where I am not welcome.

On your report card! Sorry friends!

I also feel sad when that happens.

You will have to work hard to change that!

questions.q: What is Goloo?
Which of these look like Goloo?
Why is Goloo not welcome on a report card?
choices: A zero looks like a circle

I can draw and I can make things.

pages.text: Lalu the owl was a friendly fellow. All the birds in the jungle were his friends.
But Lalu's best friend in the jungle was Sweety, the peacock.
One day Lalu organised a party and called all his friends.
In the party, all the birds danced and gifted Lalu with a crown of feathers.
Lalu slept happily that night.

pages.text: It was holiday time. Veena and Vinay were in the garden. There were tins of paint everywhere.

image.alt: Girl hanging from a tree branch and boy sitting near cans of paint

pages.text: There was white paint and red paint and green paint and blue paint and yellow paint.

image.alt: Palm on wall and handprints of different colors

pages.text: The painters were busy. One painter was on a ladder. Another was hanging from the roof on a swing. “Can we help?” asked Veena and Vinay.

The painter gave each of them a brush. “Paint the inside of the gate,” he said to Veena.

“Paint the outside of the gate,” he said to Vinay.

image.alt: Man giving a boy and a girl a paintbrush

pages.text: They picked up two tins of paint and set to work. Veena painted one side of the gate. Vinay painted the other side of the gate.

image.alt: Boy and girl painting two sides of a gate

pages.text:
The paint fell on the ground.

The paint fell on the wall.

The paint fell on them.
At last they finished. They wiped off the paint that had splashed on the ground. They wiped off the paint that had splashed on the wall.

image.alt: Girl and boy cleaning up paint

pages.text: They wiped off the paint that had splashed on them.

image.alt: Mother helping girl and boy wipe paint off themselves

pages.text: "I love my red gate!" said Veena.

image.alt: Girl standing happily next to a red gate and boy looking on

pages.text: "I love my green gate!" said Vinay.

pages.text:
“Oh, you have made a two-coloured gate!” cried the painter.

“Let us keep it that way!” said Mother.

pages.text:
Look at us.

Do you want to be our friend?

My legs are very strong.

I can run really fast with them.
And my arms... such a nice swing!

I like to draw.

I use my hands for drawing.

Should I draw your picture?

I can see you with my eyes.

The bird sings a sweet song.

I can hear it with my ears.

I think Ma is making halwa.

I can smell it with my nose.
Oh! This sugarcane is so tough! But my teeth are strong too!

It is very sweet.

My tongue just told me.

I can sing.

Should I sing you a song?

Where have you gone?

Not on the sofa.

Not under the cot.

Not in the box.

Not under my sister's frock.

pages.text:
Not under the pillow.

Not in my bag.

Sob, sob, where have you gone?

I have looked in every room,

l have looked under every book.

I have looked under the chair,

I have looked under the stool.

Where have you gone?

"Look what I found in the park."

"It can sway, it can bounce.

It can spin, it can dangle.

Ha-ha, hee-hee," said Granny with a giggle.

Oh Granny! Thank you so much!

You have found my dear yo-yo!

pages.text:

What a funny toy!

I want to play with it,

It gives me so much joy!"

image.alt: Boy and old lady playing with a yo-yo

For the rest of the day!

pages.text: I have a friend. She lives in my house.

image.alt: Two girls looking at each other through the window

pages.text: When I am happy, so is she.
When I cry, she cries too.

pages.text: Pehelwaan ji!

image.alt: Man eating a pile of rotis

He walks with a swagger.
He orders all the children about.

Both of them slapped their thighs!

pages.text: The little elephant's name was Golu. He was as round as a drum. The little rabbit was called Chhotu. He looked like a ball of cotton.

They played together.

One day, Golu said, “Let's play a new game today.”
“You sit down. I'll land on your back in one flying leap,” said Chhotu. Golu sat down. Chhotu took a mighty leap.

Thump! He landed on Golu's back.

“Wow!” laughed Golu and said, “My turn now. You sit down and I will leap on your back.”

“You!”

“Yes, me.”

“How can you do that?” asked Chhotu.

image.alt: Rabbit pointing something out to elephant

pages.text: "Like this!" Golu showed him.

Thud... thud... thud...

A shower of coconuts came down on Golu's head.
He ran away on fat legs, scared.
One small coconut fell on Chhotu.

image.alt: Coconut falling on rabbit and elephant running away

pages.text: ‘That's better,' thought Chhotu, ‘Better a coconut than an elephant on my head!'

questions.q: What did Chhotu the rabbit look like?
What fell on Golu's head?
Why was Chhotu glad that only a coconut fell on him?

pages.text: A cloud rolled along merrily in the sky.
The peacock said, “Why don't you rain? I will dance for you.”
The fish said, "Please rain. I need more water."

image.alt: Fish looking up at the cloud in the sky

pages.text: The farmer said, “Please rain. I'll plant seeds for the next crop.”

image.alt: Farmer gazing at the cloud in the sky

pages.text: Raju said, “If you rain, I'll sail paper boats.”

image.alt: Boy in the hills, with the cloud in the background

pages.text: The cloud rained in a shower of shimmering drops.
The peacock spread its pretty feathers and danced.
The pond filled up. The fish was happy.

image.alt: Fish leaping out of a pond as it rains

pages.text: The farmer started planting seeds.
Splish! Splash! Splosh! Raju and his friends had a wonderful time in the puddles.
The cloud filled everybody's heart with joy. It moved on. All the children waved goodbye.

What did Raju want to sail?

choices: The rain gave each of them what they needed

pages.text:
It is my first day at school.

Mummy is holding my hand and walking with me.

“I am grown up now,” I say. “Let go, let go!”

Mummy holds my hand very tight.

image.alt: Girl holding mother's hand at school

pages.text:
There are many children near the school.

They come by bus. They come by car.

They come by rickshaw. They cycle.

They walk, like me.

We reach the gate. Mummy lets go of my hand.

She stays at the gate. I have to go inside alone.

There are many new faces all around me.

I take one step. I take another step. I look back. Mummy gets smaller as I walk away. Will she disappear?

I run back to her. I don't feel so grown up. I hold her hand.

“Don't go away,” I say.

Everyone is inside now. I am the only one outside. The teacher comes out. She smiles at me. I smile back.

Mummy says, "Rani, I will be here when you come out."

I let go of her hand. She waves to me.
I run inside. Mummy will be there after school!

questions.q: How does Rani get to school?
Who came out and smiled at Rani?
Why did Rani run back to Mummy?
choices: She felt scared and not so grown up

pages.text: A fawn was racing in the forest.
He was ahead of the rabbit.
He was ahead of the elephant.
He leapt and cleared the stream.
He ran past the crumbling wall.
There was a large boulder on the grassy plain. He stumbled and fell down.
He burst into tears.
The monkey massaged his leg. Tears flowed from the fawn's eyes.
Brother Bear picked him up. The fawn didn't stop crying.
His mother came. She said, “Look, we'll beat up this bad boulder!”
The fawn said, “Oh, don't do that or he will also start crying.” His mother laughed. So did the fawn.

questions.q: Who did the fawn race ahead of first?
Why did the fawn fall down?
choices: He tripped over a big rock

questions.q: Why didn't the fawn want his mother to beat up the boulder?
choices: He thought the boulder would cry too
The boulder was his friend's house
He wanted to do it himself

pages.text: All of us went to the Dasara fair.
Papa bought Chintu fancy glasses. Mother bought me a bright blue cap. The baby got sugar candy.

image.alt: Children wearing fancy glasses and eating candy

pages.text:
On the way home, a very strong wind came.

It blew my cap away.

image.alt: Boy losing his cap in the wind

pages.text: My cap got stuck on a branch of the old Pipal tree.

image.alt: Boys looking at cap caught on a tree

pages.text: I cried a lot. And I did not eat my dinner.

image.alt: Boys sitting during meal and one boy crying

pages.text:
Later that night, the moon came up.

It looked at my cap on the old Pipal tree.

image.alt: Boy looking at cap caught on a tree from a window

pages.text: It tried on my cap. The moon smiled happily. I had to smile too.

image.alt: Boy looking at moon wearing a cap

pages.text: After school the next day, my mother gave me a shiny new red cap. “The moon sent it,” she said.

That night, both the moon and I wore our caps and smiled.

We were happy.

image.alt: Boy wearing a red cap and smiling moon wearing a blue cap

pages.text: Do you think the sun needs a hat?
Guess which cap I am wearing today!

glossary.note: a big outdoor market with rides and treats, here for the Dasara festival
a big tree with heart-shaped leaves

questions.q: What blew the cap away?
Where did the cap get stuck?
Why did Mother say "The moon sent it"?
choices: She found it in the sky

pages.text:
On Sunday, Manu's parents got him a red raincoat.

“Ma, may I wear it now?” asked Manu.

“No, my dear, the rains are near, but just now the sky is clear,” said Ma.

image.alt: Boy holding a red raincoat and lady talking

pages.text:
Monday was bright and sunny.

“WILL it rain today, Mummy?” asked Manu.

“No Manu, not today. If you wear your raincoat, you will look quite funny!” said Ma.

image.alt: Boy and lady looking out of the window

pages.text:
On Tuesday, the sky was blue.

“Ma, WHEN will my wish come true?” asked Manu.

“Not today, my dear, there is just one white cloud in the sky!” said Ma.

image.alt: Boy sitting on the stairs of a house with a red raincoat

pages.text:
Wednesday was hot.

“Ma, WHY doesn't it rain?” asked Manu.

“Son, I think it will rain very soon. Maybe even before it is noon,” said Ma.

image.alt: Boy wearing a red raincoat and sun shining through the window

pages.text:
On Thursday Manu went on a picnic. “Ma, WHAT if it rains? Shall I take the raincoat with me?” asked Manu.

“No my dear, it will not rain today. The little white clouds are too high in the sky,” said Ma.

image.alt: Boy holding a red raincoat and looking at the sky

pages.text:
Friday was cloudy.

“Ma, will it rain today?” asked Manu loudly.

“It might, my dear. There are some dark clouds low down in the sky,” said Ma.

image.alt: Boy with red raincoat and peacock looking at cloudy sky

pages.text:
Saturday began with a bang!

Badaboom!

"Ma, is that thunder I hear? Will it rain very soon?" asked Manu.

image.alt: Boy, snail and frog enjoying the rain

pages.text:
And then at last, it started raining!

“Oh, it's raining, it's raining,” sang Manu, running out.

image.alt: Boy and frog enjoying the rain

pages.text: “But Manu,” called Ma, running after him, “you forgot your raincoat!”

image.alt: Boy playing in the rain and lady watching

questions.q: When did Manu get his red raincoat?
On which day did the thunder come?
What is funny about the end of the story?
choices: Manu forgot his raincoat when it finally rained

pages.text:
This is Bekku.

And that is me in the mirror.

This is what I love to do

... and this is what Bekku likes to do.

This is Bekku's favorite place, and that is mine.

When Bekku sees a mouse she runs after it.

image.alt: Girl reading under a tree and cat playing

pages.text: But if I see a mouse, I run from it.
Then when I run after my beeping car, Bekku scoots out through the door ajar.

When mamma gives us milk, we both go SLURP, SLURP.

Then follow our loud BURP, BURPS!

We like different things - that is very plain.

Our common love for milk, this will always remain!

questions.q: What does Bekku do when she sees a mouse?
What do the child and Bekku both love?
What kind of animal is Bekku most likely?

pages.text:
I am Timmy.

This is my friend, Pepe, the puppy.

I like to tease Pepe.

I tell him I am better than him.

He does not like it.

“Look, I have a nose!” I say.

“Woof,” says Pepe. That means he has a nose too.

image.alt: Girl and dog pointing at nose

pages.text:
“Look, I have ears!” I say.

“Woof,” says Pepe. That means he has ears too.

image.alt: Girl and dog pointing at ears

pages.text:
“Look, I have eyes!” I say.

“Woof,” says Pepe. That means he has eyes too.

image.alt: Girl and dog pointing at eyes

pages.text:
“Look, I can dance on my legs!” I say.

“Woof, woof, woof,” says Pepe. That means he has legs too.

“Look, I have a tongue!” I say.

“Woof,” says Pepe. That means he has a tongue too.

image.alt: Girl and dog sticking out tongue

pages.text:
“I can think!” I say.

“Wooooooof,” says Pepe. That means he can think better.

“Look I have hands!” I say.

“Grrrrrr...” Pepe says, and turns to show his little tail.

That means he has a tail and I don't have one.

image.alt: Girl showing hands and dog showing tail

pages.text: But I love Pepe, the puppy and he loves me too.

In the picture above find:

* Eyes
* Hands
* Nose
* Legs
* Tongue
* Ears

questions.q: Who is Pepe?
What does Pepe have that Timmy does not?
What does Timmy learn about Pepe?
choices: They are each special, and they love each other

pages.text:
Everytime I finish my hot, hot bath,

My wet body feels so cool, cool cool.

Who makes that happen?

Vayu the Wind!

The milk in my cup is too hot, too hot.

But soon it is ready for me to gulp.

Who makes that happen?

Vayu the Wind!

image.alt: Girl blowing on cup with wind

pages.text:
The window curtains flutter

And gently brush my face.

Who makes it happen?

Vayu, the Wind!

image.alt: Girl feeling the wind through an open window

pages.text:
A bolt of lightning far away.

Black clouds moving my way.

Who makes that happen?

Vayu, the Wind!

image.alt: Wind amidst clouds and lightning bolt

pages.text:
Branches sway and leaves tremble.

Flowers gently fall.

Who did it all?

Vayu, the Wind!

Far from the house, we are playing,

Yet, I can smell the sweets mother is preparing.

Who makes it happen?

Vayu, the Wind!

image.alt: Wind and girl entering the house, racing towards sweets

pages.text:
A glass tumbler on a window sill,

Crashes on the ground.

Thank God, I was not around.

Who played this mischief?

Of course, it was Vayu, the Wind!

image.alt: Girl and smiling wind looking at a broken tumbler

pages.text:
A whistle blows. A train rolls in.

I cannot see, but I hear its din.

Who makes that happen?

Vayu, the Wind!

Cannot be seen

Cannot be heard

Does all the work

Without a word.

Who can it be?

Of course!

The wind!

Vayu, the wind!

glossary.note: a name for the wind in Hindi and Sanskrit

questions.q: Who makes the child's wet body feel cool after a bath?
What crashed on the ground?
Why can't we see Vayu?
choices: The wind is air, and we cannot see air

pages.text:
Anu loves to look at things,

big things and small.

Houses on hills,

ants on a wall.

Things in the kitchen,

things on the shelf.

Things in the garden,

things on herself.

image.alt: Things on a shelf and in a kitchen

pages.text:
Anu sees patterns

and shapes everywhere,

nothing at all can escape her stare!

Spots on a ladybird,

circles in trees,

shapes made by people,

shapes made by bees.

Lines on a leaf, just

like lines on her hand.

The marks of her feet

in wet seaside sand.

Waves in the water,

waves in her hair.

Mushrooms on tree

trunks, birds in the air.

Words in a book that

can take her to places,

full of new colours,

new stories, new faces.

image.alt: Books, ships, trees, girl and castles

pages.text:
Things of the colour that

she loves best - RED!

The three wiggly hairs on

her brother Boo's head.

image.alt: Baby looking at apple, book, flower and umbrella

pages.text:
Sprinkles on the cake

Daddy baked today,

like the stars that twinkle

at her from far away.

image.alt: Girl looking at cake outside window

pages.text:
Rabbits in clouds

floating up in the sky.

Elephants in shadows -

come, give it a try!

image.alt: Rabbits in clouds and hand shadows

pages.text:
Anu is happy with the

things that she sees.

Do you also see what

little Anu sees?

questions.q: What color does Anu love best?
What did Daddy bake?
What is Anu good at?

pages.text: Do you get the feeling sometimes that none of your clothes are just right? I do!

The shirt buttons trouble me.

The pants feel too tight on me.

The lehenga seems to trip me.

The choli does not fit me.

My salwar keeps slipping.

The golden zari keeps itching.

The churidaar pulls and tugs everywhere.

Nothing perfect seems to be there.

This frock is too bright.

Brother's T-shirt? What a funny sight!

image.alt: Girl holding frock and t shirt

pages.text:
Papa's kurta is rather long.

Mummy's sari is wrapped all wrong.

Some things are well out of my reach. Oh, it really makes me want to screech!

These clothes seem to say, ‘We shall trouble you all day.'

But I have made up my mind today...

image.alt: Girl sitting on a pile of clothes

pages.text: ... to mix and match these clothes in a way that I have my very own style today!

image.alt: Girl dressed up in front of mirror

glossary.note: a long skirt and a short top
kinds of loose and tight pants
a long piece of cloth worn wrapped as a dress

questions.q: What keeps itching?
Whose kurta is too long?
How does she solve her problem?
choices: She mixes and matches clothes in her own style

pages.text: Kicchu woke up early one morning.“It is time to catch some fish,” he said yawning.

image.alt: Boy waking up and stretching in the morning

pages.text: He met Choru on the way to the pond. They were best friends who played all day long.

image.alt: Boys holding fishing rods and talking

pages.text:
Munia saw them marching with their fishing rods.

“We are going to the pond to catch fish. Come along Munia, if you wish.”

image.alt: Girl standing behind tree and talking to two boys carrying fishing rods

pages.text: Little Munia thought for sometime. “Please don't do that,” she said, “without water, the fish will die.”

image.alt: Girl with cat talking to two boys carrying fishing rods

pages.text: They did not listen to what Munia had to say. They headed to the pond straight away.

image.alt: Girl and cat going after two boys walking ahead with fishing rods

pages.text: Kicchu and Choru sat waiting by the pond. Two fish swam across, one thin and another round.

image.alt: Girl and cat looking at two boys fishing

pages.text: Then came the third fish, the biggest one they had seen. Munia said laughing, “It is bigger than Appa's feet!”

image.alt: Two boys fishing and girl and cat, big fish nearby

pages.text:
Kicchu and Choru held on tight to their rods.

Kicchu screamed, “MY FISH!”

Choru also screamed, “NO... MY FISH!”

image.alt: Girl and cat looking at two boys fighting

pages.text:
Kicchu pulled hard...

Choru pulled harder...

image.alt: Two boys pulling hard at their fishing rods

pages.text:
PHAAATTT! Both the rods broke.

THUDDD! Kicchu fell to the ground.

SSSPPLAASH! Choru fell into the water.

image.alt: Fishing rods breaking and two boys falling down

pages.text:
What had happened?

What do you think?

The fish had tied up both the strings!

image.alt: Fish underwater holding tangled strings in their mouths

questions.q: Where were the boys going to catch fish?
Why did Munia ask them not to catch fish?
Who really played a trick in this story?

pages.text: For the very first time, Maaloo is collecting vegetables from the garden. He has collected red tomatoes, fresh brinjals and green lady's fingers.
Dadi says, “Well done, Maaloo! Go and get some potatoes too.”
Maaloo looked at all the trees, creepers and plants. Not a single potato could he see.

“Dadi, the potatoes aren't ready yet,” said Maaloo, putting the empty basket down.

“No Maaloo, there are plenty of potatoes. Look carefully,” said Dadi.

image.alt: Old woman talking to boy with basket

pages.text:
Maaloo went into the garden once more. Kaaloo followed him.

Maaloo was looking for potatoes when he heard, “Woof! Woof!”

image.alt: Boy with basket walking with dog

pages.text:
“Kaaloo! Stop, Kaaloo!” yelled Maaloo, running behind him. “Don't spoil the garden.” Maaloo saw that Kaaloo was digging away and what do you think was coming out of the mud?

Big fat potatoes!

image.alt: Boy running towards dog in a garden

pages.text: “Well done, Kaaloo. You found the potatoes!” laughed Maaloo, filling his basket with potatoes.

image.alt: Happy boy and dog looking at potatoes

questions.q: Who asked Maaloo to get potatoes?
Who found the potatoes?
Why couldn't Maaloo see the potatoes at first?

pages.text:
“Anuuuu! Wake up! Sleepyhead!” called Anu's mother.

“Mmmm...let me sleep!” mumbled Anu.

“Ok, then I'll go see Aunty Jui's baby by myself,” said Aai*.

*Aai, Marathi for mother

Anu sat up like a shot.

“Baby? Is it a teeny-tiny baby? Like a doll? Wait for me, I'm coming!”

image.alt: Girl sitting up on the bed

pages.text:
Anu got ready in a jiffy.

She gulped down her milk without a fuss.

She didn't even cry when her mother combed her hair.

The moment Anu entered Aunty's house she shouted, “Aunty! Where is the baby?”

“Shhhh...” said Aunty Jui, with her finger on her lips. “Softly. The baby is sleeping.”

Sleeping? What a bore. Anu began to sulk.

image.alt: Girl talking to a lady with a baby on her lap

pages.text:
Aai pulled Anu close. “The baby is still very small, Anu. You must not trouble her. After all, you are her big sister!”

Big sister! Anu felt very important. But why did the baby have to go to sleep?

image.alt: Lady holding girl close and talking to her

pages.text:
Just then they heard a thin wail...

“She is up,” said Aunty, and gave the baby to Aai.

“I want to hold the baby,” said Anu.

“Oh no, Anu. You won't be able to. You're much too small,” said Aai.

“But I'm her big sister,” said Anu.

image.alt: Girl and lady looking at a baby in another lady's lap

pages.text: Why should the baby sit on Aai's lap? I want to sit on Aai's lap too, thought Anu. But Aai said, “Anu, move away! You must not bother baby. See how tiny she is?”

image.alt: Lady holding a baby in her lap and speaking to a little girl

pages.text:
The baby was still wailing. “Waah...”

“Oh dear!” said Aunty. “I think she's soiled her nappy.”

She cleaned the baby and changed her nappy.

The baby gurgled happily.

image.alt: Two ladies changing a baby's nappy

pages.text:
Anu was disgusted. What a silly baby. Potty in the nappy!

And Aai and Aunty were mad! They didn't even scold the baby.
If I just pee in my underwear by mistake, Aai glares at me. But now look at her doing ‘kootchie-coo!' to the baby! Wait till I get home. I'll tell Baba how unfair Aai is.

“Let's go home, Aai!” Anu cried.

“Why, Anu, don't you like the baby?” asked Aunty. “Chee!” said Anu.

“Silly baby, does potty in the nappy, doesn't talk, doesn't play. I don't like your baby. Why did you get yourself such a silly baby?”

image.alt: Girl talking to two ladies with a baby on one's lap

pages.text:
On the way back home, Anu asked her mother, “Aai, when will I become a baby?”

“You won't become a baby again, “ said Aai. “You'll grow bigger now.”

“I don't want to be big! I want to be a baby and I want to sleep in your lap, and I want to drink milk with a spoon and I want to sit on Baba's shoulders and go out and...”

Anu muttered all the way home.

image.alt: Girl and lady in saree talking

pages.text: The next day Aai said, ”Anu, let's give your small clothes, toys and cradle to Aunty Jui's baby, shall we?”

image.alt: Girl and lady looking at toys and clothes

pages.text:
“No!” yelled Anu. “That's my ball and my cradle!”

“Okay, what about giving away these clothes then? They're so small,” said Aai.

“No!” shouted Anu again. “I want to wear them, NOW!” So Aai put the small frock on Anu. She even put the little baby bonnet on her head.

image.alt: Girl holding a ball and wearing a frock and bonnet

pages.text:
Anu crawled all over the house.

She balanced the ball on her head and wandered around, calling, ‘Curd! Fresh curd!' She played with the rattle: rat-a-tat-tat.

image.alt: Girl wearing a frock, bonnet and playing with toys

pages.text:
Anu climbed into the cradle. She wanted to lie down and suck her thumb.

But she didn't fit! Her feet stuck out at one end, and she couldn't keep her arms straight. The tight little frock began to pinch. Anu was fed up. This was no fun at all!

image.alt: Girl sitting on cradle and sucking her thumb

pages.text:
Anu said to her mother, “Aai, why don't we give this frock and bonnet and cradle to Aunty Jui's baby?”

“Give it all away? But then what will you do?” asked Aai.

“Aai, I'm a big sister now, aren't I? Once you become a big sister you wear proper clothes, and sleep on the bed.”

“Oh really? I had no idea!” said Aai, smiling.

Anu wore her own clothes and said, “Aai, tell baby that her big sister has given her all this. You'll tell her, won't you?”

Anu jumped on to her scooter and went off to play.

image.alt: Girl on scootie talking to her mother

questions.q: Why did Anu get ready so fast?
What did Anu try to lie down in?
Why did Anu decide to give her baby things away?
choices: She felt proud to be a big sister

pages.text:
Bheema loves to sleep and just cannot get up early.

Ramu, the washerman, scolds Bheema often.

One day, Gauri, the cow, asked him, “Bheema, why are you so sad?”

Bheema said, “I cannot get up early and Ramu shouts at me every day. Will you wake me up every morning, please?”

“Yes, I will,” said Gauri. Early next morning, Gauri mooed loudly, but Bheema did not wake up.

Coming back from the river in the evening, Bheema met Moti, the dog.

“I can never get up in the morning on time. Will you wake me up?” Bheema asked Moti.

“Yes, I will,” said Moti and the next morning he barked and barked but did Bheema wake up? No Sir!

That evening Bheema met Cheenu, the rooster.

He said to Cheenu, “You crow in the morning and everybody wakes up. Will you wake me up too?”

Cheenu agreed. The next morning, Cheenu crowed long and loud, but Bheema did not wake up.

The next evening, Bheema saw Kalu, the crow, cawing away happily.

“Kalu, will you wake me up in the morning, please?” he asked.

Kalu said, “Why not? I will caw and wake you up.”

The next morning Kalu cawed all he could but Bheema did not wake up.

Bheema was sad.

The next morning, a fly came and sat on his nose.

“Aaah...chhoooo... ahchhoo!” Bheema got up with a big sneeze.

“Wow! I woke up. How did I wake up?” he asked in wonder.

“I woke you up,” said the fly.“Will you wake me up like this early every morning?”

“Sure,” said the fly. Bheema was happy. Now he would have no problem getting up early every morning!

glossary.note: a person who washes clothes for other people

questions.q: Who scolds Bheema?
Who finally woke Bheema up?
Why did the fly's way of waking him work?

pages.text:
Nanhi picked up her slate and chalk.

She wanted to draw a long, l-o-n-g train.

image.alt: Girl carrying a slate and walking with dog

pages.text: Nanhi first drew an engine which gave out a lot of smoke, for the long, long train.

image.alt: Girl drawing on a slate and dog watching

pages.text: “Oh dear! Now where shall I make the coaches?” Nanhi wondered, for there was no more space on the slate.

image.alt: Girl holding slate and looking worried

pages.text: Nanhi put the slate and chalk down on the floor and thought.

image.alt: Girl and dog looking at slate

pages.text:
She drew a coach on the floor.

Then a second coach, then another, and another, and another... Nanhi just kept drawing.

Until her chalk got over.

Nanhi got up and took a look. Wow!

Her train was as long as the verandah!

image.alt: Girl and dog watching a moving train

pages.text: And off went Nanhi's train – Chhuk-Chhuk-Chhak, from here to there, so very far!

image.alt: Girl and dog running happily with train in the background

glossary.note: a small board you write on with chalk

questions.q: What did Nanhi want to draw?
Where did Nanhi draw the coaches?
Why did Nanhi stop drawing on her slate?
choices: There was no more space on it

pages.text:
It was a bright moonlit night. All the animals in Mangu's farm were sleeping.

Except Tinku!

“I am not sleepy, Ma,” murmured Tinku. But Ma did not hear him. She was fast asleep.

He turned left, and he turned right. He lay on his tummy, and rolled on his back. But he could not sleep!

So he set off into the night to see what he could find. Up in the sky, Tinku saw the moon, white and round, smiling down at him. He felt very happy.

‘Night is beautiful,' thought Tinku.

image.alt: Dog running out of farm at night

pages.text:
Far away on the top of a tree, there were some tiny lights. One spot of light flew down! “I'm a firefly,” said the spot of light. “I glow in the dark!”

“Will you be my friend?” asked Tinku.

“Yes, I will!” said the firefly.

image.alt: Dog talking to firefly at night

pages.text:
Something flew by and hung upside down on a tree.

“What is your name, bird?” asked Tinku.

“I am not a bird, I am a bat. I can see during the night!” said the bat.

“Will you be my friend?” asked Tinku.

“Yes, I will!” said the bat.

image.alt: Dog talking to bat at night

pages.text:
A few leaves moved in the bushes. Someone was hiding! “Who are you?” asked Tinku.

“I am a fox,” said the fox. “I go strolling out at night.”

“Will you be my friend?” asked Tinku.

“Yes, I will!” said the fox.

image.alt: Dog talking to fox at night

pages.text:
Two shiny eyes looked at him from a tree. “Who are you?” asked Tinku.

“I'm an owl,” said the owl. “I hunt for food during the night.”

“Will you be my friend?” asked Tinku.

“Yes, I will!” said the owl.

image.alt: Dog talking to owl at night

pages.text:
“CHIRRRRRP! CHIRRRRRP!”

“Who is here?” Tinku asked.

“I'm a cricket,” said the cricket. “I chirp when it is dark.”

“Will you be my friend?” asked Tinku.

“Yes, I will!” said the cricket.

image.alt: Dog talking to cricket at night

pages.text:
Tinku and his friends jumped and tossed and rolled until Tinku yawned. “I am sleepy. I have to go home now,” said Tinku. He was happy that he had many new friends.

Snuggling close to Ma, he said, “Night is not a lonely place, Ma. Night is full of wonderful beings.”

“Yes!” replied Ma. “Your new friends are nocturnal, just like wild dogs.”

image.alt: Dog, firefly, bat, fox, owl and cricket

pages.text: “Nocturnal animals eat, play and work at night. They rest during the day. You must sleep now. Sleep will give you energy to play with your day-time friends tomorrow. Good night, little one!” she said, hugging him tight.

The bright round moon shone all night long, spreading her calm light all around.

And Tinku slept all through the night!

image.alt: Dog and puppy sleeping at night

questions.q: Why did Tinku go out into the night?
Which new friend glows in the dark?
Ma says Tinku's new friends are nocturnal. What does that mean?

pages.text:
Nani keeps losing her glasses.

“Where did I keep them?” she always asks. Without her glasses, she cannot find her glasses.

image.alt: Girl standing on the cot, Lady standing

pages.text: So she needs me. To be her eyes, to find her own eyes!

Sometimes her spectacles are in the bathroom. Or on her bed. Or on her head.

“Nani,” I say, “they are on your head!”

image.alt: Girl behind a cot, Lady knitting

pages.text:
“Of course! How silly of me. Thank you, Richa dear,” she says with a giggle.

This time, though, I cannot find Nani's glasses. Not yet.

image.alt: Girl crouching behind a bed and watching her grandmother knit

pages.text:
I have looked everywhere. In all the usual places. On her head, in the bathroom, inside her cupboard, and on the puja shelf. I have looked under her favourite chair and on the dining table.

Nothing. No glasses. Where could they be?

image.alt: Girl under a chair, Open Cupboard

pages.text: I decided to be a good detective. I decided to find out what she had done all day.

image.alt: Women eating and drinking at the dining table, with girl standing

pages.text: “I did nothing much today. Except that Veena's mother-in-law came, you know. And how much she gossips! We had many cups of tea. And she ate all the laddoos your mother had made,” said Nani.

image.alt: Women drinking tea and having snacks at the table

pages.text: Raju said, “Nani was very busy today. She wrote a letter to the Chief Minister about her pension.”

image.alt: Woman and girl holding a sweater, Cat following a girl, lady writing a letter

pages.text:
Amma said, “She spoke for a long time to your Masi. She finished knitting the sweater for Raju. And then she went for a short walk.”

I now had many clues. I quickly looked around new places in the house.

Aha! I have found the missing glasses!

image.alt: Letter being written, Old woman and girl holding an orange sweater

pages.text:
The spectacles were wrapped in wool, kept next to her pen, under the phone, on her desk. And I found a half-eaten laddoo there as well. For Nani's next birthday, I will save money for an extra pair of glasses!

Nani: Hindi word for grandmother

Masi: Hindi word for mother's sister

image.alt: Girl looking at Telephone and Spectacles

questions.q: Where are Nani's glasses sometimes?
Where were the glasses this time?
choices: Wrapped in wool on her desk

questions.q: How did Richa find the glasses?
choices: She found out what Nani did all day, like a detective

pages.text:
It was a holiday for Amma. She was reading a book. Anil had a holiday too. He wanted to do.... SOMETHING!

“Amma, I want to see what is in that blue box!” said Anil.

“Later, Anil,” said Amma.

image.alt: Lady reading a book and boy pulling her saree

pages.text:
Anil put a stool over a chair. He climbed up to get the box down.

“No, no! Not that one! All the boxes on top of that will fall on our heads, Anil!” said Amma.

image.alt: Lady yelling at a boy pulling heavy boxes from a shelf

pages.text: Anil was very angry. He was angry with his mother.
“Come, let's go to the market and get you something,” said Amma.

image.alt: Lady going shopping and holding a boy's hand

pages.text:
Anil was very angry even after they went to the market.

“I want that one!” he said, pointing at an orange.

“No, no, not that one! The fruits will all fall down!” said the shopkeeper.

image.alt: Mother and son shopping at a vegetable market

pages.text:
“I want that book!” said Anil.

“No, no, not that one!” said the shopkeeper.“Take this one.”

image.alt: Man looking at boy trying to pull out a book from a pile

pages.text:
“I want that one!” shouted Anil, almost pulling out a samosa from a high stack of samosas.

“No, no, not that one!” warned the shopkeeper.

“All my samosas will fall to the ground!”

image.alt: Boy trying to pull out a samosa from a pile and man shouting

pages.text:
“I want that one!” said Anil loudly. He was now in a very, very bad mood.

“No, no, not that one!” said the flower seller. “Don't touch them! They will wilt.”

image.alt: Boy pointing at flowers and crying while flower seller looks on

pages.text: By now, Anil was crying loudly. Everyone was looking at Anil.

“I want that one! The black one!” said Amma loudly.

Anil stopped crying suddenly.

“Amma, no, no! Not that one!” said Anil.

image.alt: Lady in saree pointing at something

pages.text:
“Let's take this brown one!” said Anil. Then Anil gently lifted the brown puppy on top of a pile of puppies.

“Amma, I am very angry with you! All the puppies would have fallen down!”

Amma smiled. Anil was smiling too. He was not angry at all now.

image.alt: Boy holding a puppy and a pile of puppies in a basket

glossary.note: a fried pastry filled with potatoes

questions.q: What did Anil want to see first?
choices: What was in the blue box

questions.q: Why did the shopkeeper say no to the samosa?
Why did Anil feel better at the end?
choices: He picked a puppy carefully and saw why people said no

pages.text:
“Meenu, please get a glass of water for Manoj,” says Amma. Manoj Mama has come to take me to Ooty!

“We will go by train, Meenu. It is cold in Ooty even during summer, as it is in the hills,” he says.

image.alt: Girl handing a glass of water to her parents

pages.text:
Summer is the season between spring and monsoon. It is called Greeshma Ritu in Sanskrit. School has closed for the summer.

My friends and I do not mind playing outside. But our parents do not like us to play in the hot sun. So we sit under the trees and eat fruits and tell stories.

image.alt: Children sitting below a tree and eating fruits

pages.text:
Yesterday was new year's day for my family. We call it Varsha Porappu in Tamil. Why are there so many new year's days in the same year?

Grandma made raw mango panna. So sweet and tangy! Jasmit's mother made lassi. So cool and creamy! Last month, Farhan's aunty made falooda for their new year. So milky and sweet-smelling!

Appa has gone to Delhi. He says it is very hot and dusty there. In earlier times, people put mats made of khus on windows and kept them wet to cool their homes. Appa wears dark glasses to shade his eyes.

image.alt: Man carrying briefcase and wearing shades

pages.text: He told us that he had to drink lots of nimbu pani to replace the water in his body because you sweat a lot in the heat of Delhi. He says he will bring lovely Dussehri mangoes for us from Delhi. The summer brings heat and dust but it also brings mangoes!

image.alt: Man in a shop drinking fruit juice

pages.text: Do you remember the little sapling I planted in spring? It is my friend. It is growing up. It has seventeen leaves now. I water the little tree twice every day in summer.

I think it is waiting for the rain.

Will it bear a fruit for me next summer?

glossary.note: a sweet milk dessert with noodles

questions.q: Where is Manoj Mama taking Meenu?
What will Appa bring back from Delhi?
Why does Meenu water her little tree twice a day?
choices: It is hot summer and there is no rain yet
It is a very big tree
It is her job at school

pages.text:
There was a mouse in the house. Grandma saw it first.
"Mouse!" she screamed, jumping up the sofa. The cushions fell on the floor.

image.alt: Grandmother on sofa, pointing to a mouse

pages.text: “Where?” asked Pa, climbing up the window. He pulled the curtains down. “There!” shouted Ma, leaping up the table. The plates fell with a crash.

image.alt: Man and woman alarmed as mouse gets on the table

pages.text:
“Catch him!” said Mithun to the cat. The cat looked at the mouse and fled under the bed!
“Mouse!” screamed Mithun, running behind the cat.

image.alt: Boy and cat trying to catch the mouse

pages.text:
“I will chase it out!” said Ma bravely. She took out the broom and poked here and there. “Mouse!” shouted Pa. “Behind you!”
Ma looked at the mouse, and fled under the bed!

image.alt: Mother trying to chase the mouse with a broom

pages.text: "I know what to do!" shouted Grandma jumping down from the sofa. She rolled up a newspaper and poked here and there.

image.alt: Grandmother with a rolled up newspaper in her hand

pages.text:
“Mouse!” yelled Pa, climbing the window even higher.
“To your left!” Grandma looked at the mouse, and fled under the bed.

image.alt: Family searching for something under the bed

pages.text: “Oh no!” said Pa softly. He couldn't go any higher. He climbed down carefully, and fled under the bed before the mouse could see him!
"Mouse in the House!" shouted everyone together. That woke Baby up. She sat up on her mat, rubbing her eyes sleepily. What was that on her pillow?

image.alt: Baby laughing at the sight of a mouse

pages.text:
It had two eyes, four feet, and a long tail.
"Mouse!" said Baby, clapping happily. Baby looked at the mouse, and the mouse fled, with Baby right behind him!
Leaping up the sofa, climbing the window, jumping up the table, tumbling over the cushions...
... running in between the curtains, scurrying over the plates, and out of the door!

questions.q: Who saw the mouse first?
What did the cat do when it saw the mouse?
What is funny about this story?
choices: The grown-ups were scared but the baby was not

pages.text:
Shanti and Arun were good friends. They had so much fun together.

They shared secrets in class. They ran races on the way home.

She was always cheerful.

One day, Shanti came into the classroom slowly. Her head was bent. She looked sad. “Did someone scold you?” asked Arun.

Shanti shook her head. She sat down and did not look up. She did not answer ‘Present!' when Sona Miss called her name. Sona Miss called again, louder this time, “Shanti Kumar!” Shanti raised her hand.

image.alt: Teacher taking attendance and girl raising her hand

pages.text:
“Do you have a sore throat?” her teacher asked her. Shanti shook her head.

Her cheeks were red and it looked like she had a fever.

“Are you feeling okay?” Sona Miss asked.

Shanti nodded, still not daring to look up.

image.alt: Teacher with hand on sad girl's forehead

pages.text:
“Why does Shanti look so sad?”

“Is your little brother okay?”

“Is your puppy okay?”

“Is your grandmother okay?”

Shanti kept nodding her head to each of her friends. But she did not look up.

image.alt: Girl looking sad and friends looking at her

pages.text:
Arun wanted to make her smile. He had an idea! He took out something from his bag.

As he ran to show it to Shanti, it slipped out of his hands. Shanti saw something flying towards her and she grabbed it.

image.alt: Boy and girl looking at something in the air

pages.text:
It was a BIG, green, rubber frog!

Shanti's eyes flew open. Then she opened her mouth to laugh.

THEN Arun and her friends saw why she had not smiled or talked all day!

Four of her front teeth had gone missing!

image.alt: Girl holding a frog and laughing

questions.q: Who were good friends?
What did Arun want to show Shanti?
Why didn't Shanti smile or talk all day?
choices: She did not want anyone to see her missing teeth

pages.text:
I asked Ajji, “May I please have some laddoos?”

“Not now, beta, maybe tomorrow.”

But I did not want to wait till tomorrow.

I asked Ajja, “May I go out to play with my friends?”

“Not now, beta. Maybe after your nap?”But I did not want to wait till after my nap.

I asked Ma, “May I wear these new clothes?”

“Not now, beta, you can wear them when we go out.” But I did not want to wait till we went out.

image.alt: Boy standing next to shirt and cap

pages.text:
I asked Papa, “May I open that nice

looking box?”

“Not now, not now. You must wait.”

But I did not want to wait any more.

image.alt: Boy with father and a gift box

pages.text:
Why do big people always say,

‘Not now, not now'?

That night, I went to sleep feeling angry.

image.alt: Boy lying in bed at night

pages.text: The next day, I woke up early and went into the kitchen. Ajji said, “You can eat these laddoos now.”

Ajja said, “We can play cricket now.”

Ma said, “You can wear these clothes now.”

Papa said, “You can open this box now.” And they all said, “Happy birthday!”

glossary.note: a kind word for a child, like "dear"

questions.q: What did the child ask Ajji for?
How did the child feel when going to sleep?
Why did everyone say "Not now"?
choices: They did not like the child
They were saving things for a birthday surprise

pages.text:
Once upon a time there was a little girl called Ramya. Ramya loved earrings. Everybody who gave her gifts, gave her earrings. She had red earrings, blue earrings, green earrings, and earrings of all the colours in the rainbow.

Then, for Ramya's birthday, do you know what her Grandma got her?
Grandma got Ramya really pretty diamond earrings that looked like stars! Ramya loved them. "Oh! Grandma, from where did you get such pretty diamond stars?" she asked.

It was a starless night, and Grandma pointed to the sky. "See, there are no stars in the sky any longer. I plucked all the stars from the sky and chose the best ones for your earrings," Grandma replied.

This made Ramya very sad.

"Twinkle, twinkle little star,

How I wonder where you are?

Up above the world so high,

Please come back like diamonds in the sky!"

Ramya sang unhappily.

image.alt: Girl looking at moon from window

pages.text:
That night, Ramya took off her earrings and placed them carefully under her pillow. She hoped a fairy would return the stars to the sky.

In the middle of the night, Ramya had a beautiful dream.

In the dream, a pretty fairy came and told Ramya, “Don't worry Ramya, I have thousands of new stars for the sky!”

Ramya woke up, and do you know what she saw?
The night sky was filled with stars!

image.alt: Girl with teddy bear under the night-sky

pages.text: Ramya's eyes sparkled as she put on her precious diamond star earrings again!
Now, Ramya is so happy!

questions.q: What did Ramya love?
Where did Ramya put her earrings that night?
Why did Ramya feel sad?
choices: She thought the sky had no stars because of her earrings

pages.text:
Grandpa was writing a letter. Ritu stood beside him, leaning on the arm of the old chair.

“Grandpa, have you asked Aunty to send Mani to our home for the holidays?”

“Of course, dear Ritu, I have written to your Aunty. Look here, let me read out the letter - Dear Pooja, Hope you are fine. Mani must be having holidays now. Ritu is very eager to see him. Do send him here to Tumkur.”

Ritu jumped up and down. And since she could not stop herself, she ran around the room once and hugged Grandpa.

“Would you like to post this letter yourself?” asked Grandpa.

Ritu's eyes opened wide. “All by myself? Oh, may I?”

“Yes, little Ritu. See, I have written the address. Take it to the Post Office. Give the postcard to Ramesh Uncle. You do know that big uncle with the big, handle-bar moustaches, don't you?”

“Yes Grandpa. He is the uncle who taught Mani how to ride the cycle last summer. Will he take the letter to Aunty Pooja?” asked Ritu.

“No, dear. But the letter will reach your aunty, don't worry.”

Ritu picked up her little pink bag. She put the postcard inside. She put a pencil inside too. She felt very important.

Ritu felt very grown-up. And just a wee bit scared: what if Bageera the dog chased her?

But Ritu was very eager to post the letter. So she left for the post office that was just four buildings away!

After taking a few steps,

Ritu stopped and took out the letter. She could not read Grandpa's handwriting very well. She tried to remember what Grandpa had read.

Then, after the word that she thought was ‘Tumkur' Ritu wrote, ‘PLEECE.' Happy with her work, Ritu walked on.

image.alt: Girl writing a letter and dog watching

pages.text: After she had reached the next building, Ritu stopped and took out the postcard once again. What if Pooja Aunty did not realise how eager Ritu was to see Mani? So Ritu took out her pencil again and wrote, ‘PLEEEESE.'

image.alt: Girl writing letter with a dog by her side

pages.text: Finally, Ritu reached the small post office. There was a red post box outside the post office. Ritu could not reach the mouth of the post box even if she stood on her toes.

image.alt: Girl posting a letter at post office

pages.text:
She walked boldly up to Uncle Ramesh. He took the postcard from her and smiled. “Smart girl! Now run back to your house carefully. I shall make sure your letter reaches your aunty.”

But Ritu did not run out. She saw Uncle Ramesh pick up a pen and scribble something on the card. Then he gave it to the postman who was stamping many letters with the postmark.
Dhhum, dhhum, DHHUM, he pounded on the letters. When he saw Ritu's letter, he stopped. Then he smiled. He picked out a pencil from behind his ear and wrote something on the card.

Five days passed. The postman brought a letter to Grandpa. Grandpa read it with a smile. “Ritu, your aunty says she will send Mani here day-after. Let me read out the letter.

Dear Father...

tara...ra...ra...da...

ta...da...da...dada...

I am sending Mani tomorrow. He will reach Tumkur on Friday. I think Ritu must be very eager to see him. Your letter was very interesting...”

“Grandpa, I wrote ‘PLEECE' on the letter, that's why!” said Ritu in excitement.

“.... Your postcard had twenty ‘Please's written all over it!”

Ritu did not know how one ‘please' had become twenty.

She was just happy she had added one ‘PLEECE' And another ‘PLEEEESE!'

Pleese Pleece

PLEASE PLIS pleej

pleece Please

pleej PLIS pleece

PLEASE Pleeese PLEASE

questions.q: Who did Grandpa write the letter to?
What word did Ritu add to the letter?
Why did the letter end up with so many "please"s?
choices: The people at the post office added more

pages.text:
One afternoon, Saboo was playing alone in the garden “Mother can I have a small puppy?”

“No,” said mother.

“A very small puppy?”

asked Saboo.

“No,” said mother.
Saboo kicked a stone, which rolled near a tree. The tree trunk had fur. He touched it and looked up, up, and right up. He saw two eyes looking down at him.

“Hello! Who are you?” asked a surprised Saboo.

“Hello yourself, I am a giraffe. My name is Jojo. I can play with you. If you climb up on to my back, I will take you for a ride.”

image.alt: Giraffe and boy looking at each other

pages.text:
Saboo climbed up and away they went down the road, up the hill, and into town.

Saboo shouted happily,

“Jojo turn right, now left, and again right,” till they came to his friend Munni's house.
It was Munni's birthday. The children clapped when they saw Saboo on Jojo's back. Jojo helped Aunty put up the balloons. He was soooo...o tall, it was easy for him.

image.alt: A giraffe at a children's party

pages.text:
Jojo gave the children rides, he even played kick ball with them. It was a fun party.

Everyone sang, “Happy birthday to you.” Aunty put samosas, gulab jamuns, and ice-creams on the table.

image.alt: Happy boy on top of a giraffe

pages.text:
Jojo loved the ice-cream, so uncle got him a bucketful of ice-cream. Jojo finished it all. It was time to go home.

They said, “Bye Jojo, bye Saboo.”

Saboo and Jojo made their way back home. Mother was standing at the gate.

image.alt: Young boy clinging to a giraffe's neck

pages.text:
When she saw Saboo riding a giraffe, she was so... so... shocked.

“Saboo... I... said,”

“Mother you said, no small puppy, you did not say, no big tall giraffe.” Before mother could answer, the zookeeper came and took Jojo back to the zoo.

image.alt: Worried woman and smiling boy at the gate

questions.q: What did Saboo ask his mother for?
Where did Jojo take Saboo?
Why did Saboo think the giraffe was okay?
choices: Mother only said no to a small puppy

pages.text:
Susheela lives in Tamil Nadu.

She learnt to draw kolams from her mother.
Every Pongal, she was allowed to make one kolam all by herself.

image.alt: Girl drawing a kolam and hen watching

pages.text:
Susheela loved to make kolams!

She drew them on floors and steps and walls...

image.alt: Girl drawing kolams on floors, walls and stairs

pages.text: ... on trains and on the sides of tall buildings...

... even on kites that skipped in the sky.

Everyone admired Susheela's kolams!

image.alt: Girl and boy flying kites on terrace with kolam designs

pages.text:
One day, the Air Force asked her to help them make a kolam!

Susheela told the pilots how to dip, dive and turn their planes...

image.alt: Girl and pilots with a kolam design on a paper

pages.text: ... and in minutes there was a big, beautiful and colourful kolam in the sky, that everyone in the city could see!

image.alt: Girls looking at the sky which has the design of a kolam made by planes

pages.text:
That night, Susheela stood on her terrace and looked up at the sky. She saw the stars twinkling down at her.

Where do you think Susheela will make her next kolam?

image.alt: Girl and bird looking at starry night sky with kolams

pages.text:
Know more about Kolams...

Kolams are beautiful patterns made freehand or by joining dots. People decorate the outside of their homes with kolams to welcome a new day. They are also thought to bring good luck. Traditionally, the powder used to make kolams is made out of rice flour.

Kolams are also known as Moggu, Rangoli, Chowkpurna, Alpana and Hase Chittara. What do you call a kolam in your part of the country?

glossary.note: a pattern drawn on the ground with rice flour or chalk, made of dots and lines
a harvest festival in the state of Tamil Nadu
a flat rooftop where people can sit

questions.q: Who taught Susheela to draw kolams?
Who asked Susheela to help them make a kolam?
How did the planes make a kolam in the sky?
choices: They flew the way Susheela told them to

pages.text:
In a small garden in the city, there was a big pipal tree.

A family of squirrels lived on that tree. Vikki is one member of that family who likes to talk big. His cousin, Kato had come to visit him from Far Forest.

“Today we shall go on a big boat,” said Vikki to Kato.

“B... B... But, I... I...am afraid of water, I cannot swim,” mumbled Kato.

“Come on, you scrappy squirrel! With Vikki around, you need not be afraid. I have been on a boat many times.”

Vikki importantly leading the way, they reached the river.

image.alt: Squirrels talking in front of Pipal Tree

pages.text: The boat was tied to a post. So they ran up the rope, hopped into the boat, and sat curled in a corner.

image.alt: Squirrels running on a rope to a boat

pages.text:
Slowly the boat started moving up and down the river, which curled and curved through the trees. Kato saw many ducks swimming past them.

The fish put their heads out of the water and gulped a “Hello!”

Some swans majestically glided near them.

image.alt: Squirrels on a boat, seeing fishes and swans

pages.text:
They were so beautiful that Kato tried to touch one and he toppled over into the river. As he went deeper into the water, he passed some fish.

“Help! Help!” he gurgled, as he passed the boat.

image.alt: Squirrel and fishes look as another squirrel falls into water

pages.text:
Vikki did not know what to do. He just scampered from one side of the boat to the other side, shouting, “Help! Squirrel overboard!”

A swan had seen Kato fall into the water. She just put her head down in the water and picked up Kato in her beak. Then she tossed him into the boat.

image.alt: Swan with squirrel in the beak, Squirrels on the boat

pages.text:
A shivering, trembling Kato sat in a sunny corner to dry himself.

Vikki sat quietly near him. As he got warm and dry, he cheered up, “What an adventure! Wait till I tell the folks back home.”

Already he fancied himself as a sailor! A hero! Brave and adventurous!

image.alt: Squirrel thinking of a sailing squirrel

pages.text:
When the boat reached the bank, the squirrels hopped off and swaggered their way home. Kato was finding it difficult to keep his grand adventure inside his head. His head was going round and round like the boat.

He shut his eyes and fell fast asleep at the dinner table.

glossary.note: a big tree with heart-shaped leaves

questions.q: Who was Kato?
Who saved Kato from the water?
Was Vikki as brave as he said?
choices: No, he did not know what to do
Yes, he jumped in to save Kato

pages.text:
"Please Ma, may I help you make scarecrows?" asked Gauri.

Ma was tying some sticks together to make a scarecrow. She put an old shirt over the sticks, and then stuffed it with hay.

Gauri walked to the clothesline where the washed clothes were drying. She picked up a dress.

"I will dress her up in my new red frock and tie her hair with red ribbons too! She will look so lovely!"

image.alt: Girl looking at dress near clothesline

pages.text:
“You silly girl. You can't have a pretty scarecrow. Scarecrows have to scare the birds away, and so they must look scary! Like this!” said Mother, making a face and waving her arms.

Gauri giggled. “You look so funny Ma!”

image.alt: Girl laughing at lady making faces

pages.text: Mother took the scarecrows into the fields and fixed them amidst the tall stalks of grain. "There now, be good scarecrows and chase the birds away," said Gauri, patting them.

image.alt: Girl and lady making a scarecrow

pages.text:
Gauri and her mother returned to their hut.

Gauri went inside and lay on her cot.

A big yellow moon was rising, bathing the field in a soft, white glow.

image.alt: Girl looking at scarecrows in a field

pages.text:
Gauri saw a scarecrow look down at its clothes.

“Why do we always have to wear these tattered old clothes?” said a scarecrow with a sigh. “I wish we had something pretty to wear!”

“Yes, me too!” said another. The scarecrows looked around the field. Suddenly, one of them called out, “Hey, look at those lovely clothes flapping in the breeze. Why don't we wear those?”

“Oo-oo! These clothes are so pretty. Let us try them on!” said another.

image.alt: Girl looking at scarecrows through a window

pages.text: One scarecrow tried on a lovely red dress with sequins on them. It sparkled in the moonlight. She tied the pretty red ribbons that were flapping in the breeze on her straw hair. Thrilled with her new clothes she began to show them off.

Soon, all the scarecrows were busy dressing up! They began to parade. They walked! They turned! They twisted! They twirled!

They tossed their empty mud-pot heads, and smiled their crooked mud-pot smiles. They were having a wonderful time!

At the same time, hundreds of birds flew down to the fields. Birds here, birds there, birds everywhere. Beaks smacking! Beaks munching! Beaks chomping!

"Mmm! This is delicious!" said one, as she wiped her beak with her wing.

“It is not everyday that we can eat in the fields, without being shooed away by the scarecrows.” The scarecrows heard this and looked around. They were horrified!

“Shoo! Be gone!” they shouted at the birds, waving their straw hands wildly, to and fro.

Gauri screamed. Her mother came running.“Gauri, Gauri, what is the matter? Wake up!”

“Oh Ma, the birds! They are eating up all the grain.”

Her mother held her tight, and said, “Shh, my child! Look at the fields. They are safe! It must be a bad dream.”

Gauri looked out.

She saw the scarecrows, standing just where they were placed.

Oh, wait a minute, were they waving to her? She looked closer.

She saw a red ribbon fluttering on a scarecrow's hair. She blinked and looked again. Did the scarecrow just wink at her?

questions.q: What did Gauri want the scarecrow to wear?
What did the birds do while the scarecrows paraded?
Was the scarecrow parade real?

pages.text:
Anaya's most favorite thing in the world is her thumb. She loves her round, thick and blobby thumb as it sits in her mouth. She sucks it in bed, she sucks it in class and she sucks it on the swing. She sucks it all the time!

Her parents don't like it much and are always saying, ‘Your thumb smells', ‘Anaya stop!', ‘Anaya don't!'

Anaya is at the zoo today. Her parents do not look at her thumb since they are busy looking at the animals. Anaya sees an elephant. She spots a calf that is not splashing with his mother. He is not trumpeting with his father. He is not eating bananas with his friends. What is the baby elephant doing? Sucking his trunk!CHUSK! CHUSK!

Just ahead are some deer. Anaya sees a fawn that is not munching with her mother. She is not looking at other animals like her father. She is not prancing with her friends.

What is the baby deer doing? Sucking her hoof! CHUSK! CHUSK!

Next, the monkeys call out. Anaya spots an infant who is not clinging to her mother. She is not playing the clown with her father. She is not playing hide and seek with her friends.

What is the baby monkey doing? Sucking her thumb! CHUSK! CHUSK!

Anaya spots hippos in the water. She sees a hippopotamus calf that is not yawning wide with her mother. She is not grunting with her father. She is not swimming with her friends.

What is the baby hippo doing? Sucking her lip!CHUSK! CHUSK!

The tigers welcome her with a growl. And look at that tiger cub! He is not snoozing with his mother. He is not swatting flies with his father. He is not sneaking up on his friends.

What is the baby tiger doing? Sucking his tail! CHUSK! CHUSK!

Anaya sits down and thinks of the baby animals that are missing all the fun. Anaya looks at the people around her. She sees a boy on his father's shoulders waving his arms. She sees a boy carrying cotton candy and a juice can.

She sees a girl clicking pictures with a camera. She sees a baby shaking her rattle. All the children are having fun! Anaya looks down her nose and sees her own hand curled up, with the thumb in her mouth. Could she put her thumb to better use?

Anaya pulls her thumb out of her mouth, runs ahead and stops between her parents. She holds onto their hands, counts 1-2-3, jumps up and swings high in the air.“WHEEE!”

And the little baby monkey watching her from above does the same.

questions.q: What is Anaya's favorite thing?
What is the baby elephant sucking?
Why does Anaya take her thumb out of her mouth?
choices: She sees she is missing the fun

pages.text:
I can see big, black clouds in the sky and I can hear BADABOOM, the roll of thunder.

The monsoon is here. It is called Varsha Ritu in Sanskrit. I love the smell of wet earth. After a long hot summer, the soil also loves the first raindrops I think.

The rain makes beautiful patterns on the ground. My uncle has kept big drums in some places to save rain water. The rain water from the terrace comes and falls into these drums. So I call them waterfalls!

image.alt: Girl looking at rain water collecting in drums and man standing with umbrella

pages.text:
Aunty likes to sing aloud when it starts raining. Shubha aunty who lives in Varanasi, taught me some lovely songs called ‘Kajari'.

Do you know, Miyan Tansen, a very famous singer in the court of Emperor Akbar, could bring the rain down from the skies just by singing a song in raag ‘Miyan ki Malhar!'

I am going to start learning Indian classical music too.

image.alt: Girl and lady playing musical instrument

pages.text:
I got wet in the rain when I came running back from school, but it was fun. I saw peacocks dancing in the fields near our house. They never seem to get wet!

I cannot wait to sit on the swing that Manu has put up on the big tree, and feel the cool rainy breeze on my face.

image.alt: Girl looking at peacocks dance in the rain

pages.text:
I can smell the pakodas being fried in the kitchen. Can I be greedy and eat some corn too? Amma makes us drink hot milk.

Yesterday, she had made spicy puffed rice. And tomorrow, she says she will make puris!

image.alt: Girl and boy sniffing aroma from kitchen

pages.text:
All the trees and plants will look green and happy. Just like the green dupatta that Hari bhaiya sent for me from Jaipur. He said it is called a ‘dhaani chunariya.'

‘Dhaani' means the fresh green colour of paddy saplings. Grandpa told me that good rain means the farmers will get a good crop. We all wait for the rains, but farmers worship the rain gods.

My mango tree has grown very tall during the monsoon season. I do not have to water it at all! And when the wind blew hard last month, my tree stood firm. When will my mango tree be as big as this one?

image.alt: Girl hugging tree in the rain

glossary.note: crispy fried snacks made with vegetables and chickpea flour

questions.q: Which season is this story about?
What is being fried in the kitchen?
Why doesn't she have to water her mango tree?
choices: The tree does not need water

books.title: Samira Goes Shopping

pages.text:
Amma had just begun to make some halwa for Samira's birthday when she found that there was no sooji.

“Will you please run down to that shop and buy some sooji, dear?” said Amma pointing to the shop at the corner of the street, and gave her some money.

“Here are twelve rupees. Ask for half a kilo of sooji. Take Mouchak with you, and don't talk to any strangers on the way,” she said.

“And don't go climbing trees,” she added as Samira set out with Mouchak to buy half a kilo of sooji.

It was a pleasant February day. Samira sang, “Tra la la la la,” as she skipped along.

“Woof! Woof!” said Mouchak friskily.

They had just reached the corner when Samira saw a butterfly.

“Oh! How lovely! Let us try and catch it,” she said, and both of them ran after the butterfly.

image.alt: Girl taking a stride, Dog looking at Butterfly

pages.text: It went and sat on a baramasi flower, but away it flew exactly when Samira reached out to it. “Oh, oh!” she said sadly, then remembered that it wasn't right to catch butterflies anyway. They should be free.

A brown cat with grey stripes ran across and Mouchak began to chase it, saying, “Bow wow, bow wow wow!” And behind Mouchak ran Samira, breathless. The brown-and-grey cat leapt over a wall and disappeared. Mouchak and Samira stopped, looked at each other and laughed.

image.alt: Girl looks on as Dog chases Cat

pages.text: Then Samira saw a chandni bush. ‘Aren't the flowers like stars in the night sky? How happy Amma will be to have them,' she thought, and plucked a lot of chandni flowers.

Mouchak sniffed at them and turned away. He had found something more exciting ahead!

“Hey, where are you off to?” asked Samira, but all she got was, “Woof, woof, woof,” as Mouchak bounded off joyfully. He had found a bone and he held it out proudly to Samira. Wasn't that nice?

image.alt: Dog chewing a bone near a bush

pages.text: They had reached a great simal tree a-twitter with parrots and bulbuls. The ground below was carpeted with hundreds of rich scarlet flowers. Delighted, Samira filled her pinafore with the waxy blossoms. Her arms full of flowers, she looked up and realized that she didn't know where she was.

image.alt: Girl collecting flowers near a tree

pages.text:
She looked right and she looked left, she looked ahead and she turned on her heel, but everything was new. Samira was lost. She sat down on the pavement and began to cry, “I want to go home. I want Amma.”

Mouchak ran up and down and said, “Woof! Woof,” which meant, “Don't worry,” but Samira didn't understand and kept crying.

image.alt: Girl sitting on the pavement and crying

pages.text: Then Mouchak pulled at her dress saying, “Bow bow,” (which meant “Come, come,”) till at last she looked up and dabbed her eyes. Off they both went then, Samira sniffing a little and dropping half her flowers.

She ran behind Mouchak, turning left and turning right, up one street and down another, and soon they were home. Amma was standing at the gate, looking up and down anxiously. “Where have you been?” she asked, looking at Samira's tear-stained face.
And Samira told Amma how she had got lost and how Mouchak had brought her home. “Good dog,” said Amma, and gave him a nice big biscuit as Mouchak buried his bone in the garden.

Just then, Samira remembered that she was clutching a bunch of flowers in her hand. “Oh, Amma, these are for you,” she held out the chandni flowers. One simal blossom was sticking out of her pocket too.

“These are lovely!” said Amma. “Thank you so much. But where is the sooji?”

Amma is going to make kheer now as there is no sooji for the halwa. Samira loves kheer too. And isn't Mouchak lucky? He'll have a huge bowl of kheer in the evening with his juicy bone.

questions.q: What did Amma send Samira to buy?
Who brought Samira home?
Why will Amma make kheer instead of halwa?
choices: Samira forgot to buy the sooji
